action_items.text: A will put the minutes of the meeting on the project share and do so after every meeting.
Everyone should review the minutes from the last meeting, which are available on the project share.
D will continue with their presentation despite technical issues with their computer.
A will check if the beep feature to locate the remote control is feasible and implement it.
C will investigate the feasibility of a text-only TV guide preview on the remote control.
Everyone will do individual work after the lunch break to come up with a components concept and do trend-watching.
B will present their ideas on the design of the remote control in the next meeting.
C will look into the feasibility of making the remote control universal and how to invoke more complicated functions of a TV.
C will try to find information about the cost and feasibility of a rechargeable remote control and a docking station for recharging.
C will try to find out what people are willing to pay for the remote control features.
C will look into the feasibility of including an L_C_D_ screen and speech recognition, including cost and space requirements.
B will draw up some designs of possible remote control layouts and share them on the product share.
Everyone will try to think of a name for the remote control product.

decisions.text: Agreement to start the meeting without the marketing director, as they were late.
Agreement that the remote control should have a beep feature to help users locate it.
Agreement to hide less important functions like teletext, display settings, and audio settings under a menu.
Agreement that the remote control should have a durable design to prevent faded symbols.
Agreement to make the remote control more user-friendly by reducing the number of buttons and making important buttons larger.
Agreement to consider using changeable covers for the remote control to appeal to a broader audience and for fashion trends.
Agreement to not implement speech recognition in the remote control due to technological immaturity and international market challenges.
Agreement to make the remote control universal to cater to a wide range of users.
Agreement to focus on intuitive user interface design with fewer buttons and a secondary menu for advanced settings.
Agreement that the remote control should not look like other brands' remote controls to stand out.
Agreement to explore the feasibility of invoking TV menus through the remote control.
The power button should be on top of the remote control.
The mute button should be at the bottom of the remote control.
The channel buttons should be on top of the remote control.
The basic functions (power, channel buttons, volume, mute) should be prioritized and placed prominently.
The remote control should have a design that is easy to use and intuitive, with important buttons being larger and more accessible.
The remote control should include a feature to help locate it (e.g., beep or flash) for people who might lose it.
The remote control should be designed to be user-friendly for younger users (under 40), considering features like an L_C_D_ screen and speech recognition.
The group will decide on the final design layout for the remote control, including the placement of the volume and channel controls.
The group will consider the feasibility and cost of including an L_C_D_ screen and speech recognition, and decide based on market research and financial information.
The meeting will be concluded, and the minutes will be posted on the web shortly.
